scenario: AITA for reducing my tip to compensate for a drink I didn’t order? (US) | So short story, at a restaurant today for lunch I got an entree and a glass of water (not fancy water mind you, just tap and it didn’t even have ice). My girlfriend got the same entree and a tea. When the cheque came we had been charged the same amount, $10 for the entree and $2 for a “beverage”. When I pointed this out to the waitress she said water was a beverage and I needed to pay for it. When it came time to tip time I did the math for what I would usually tip, $2.50 tip for my $10 entree and then subtracted the price of the $2 tap water. Basically I left a .50 cent tip. My girlfriend thinks it was an asshole move and I think I’m not paying $2 for lukewarm tap water. basically I brought my cheque total to the $12.50 it would have originally been without the water added.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to reduce my tip at a restaurant because I didn't order a drink. Let me start by understanding the situation better. So, I went to a restaurant with my girlfriend for lunch. We both got the same entree, and I got a glass of water. My girlfriend also got a glass of water. When the bill came, it said $10 for the entree and $2 for a beverage for each of us. That means the total was $24, right? But I didn't order a drink, just water. I pointed this out to the waitress, and she said that water is considered a beverage and I needed to pay for it. Hmm, that seems a bit odd to me. I mean, I just wanted water, not anything fancy. It wasn't even iced. So, I think it's unfair that they charged me $2 for something that's just tap water. I mean, isn't water supposed to be free? Or at least not charged as a separate item? When it came time to tip, I usually tip about 25% on my meal. So, for my $10 entree, that would be $2.50. But since I was charged $2 for water that I didn't order, I decided to subtract that from my tip. So, I ended up leaving a 50-cent tip. My girlfriend thinks that was a bad move, but I feel like I'm not paying $2 for lukewarm tap water. Wait, but is it really my place to adjust the tip based on what I think is fair? I mean, the restaurant is charging me for a service, and I'm supposed to tip based on the service I received, not necessarily the price of the items. So, maybe I shouldn't have subtracted the $2 from my tip. On the other hand, I feel like the restaurant was overcharging me by including the water as a separate item. I didn't ask for anything special, just plain water. So, maybe it's justified to adjust the tip accordingly. I'm also thinking about the impact of tipping on the staff. If I leave a lower tip because I'm upset about the charge, does that affect the waitress's earnings? She might not have control over the pricing, so penalizing her with a lower tip might not be fair. But then again, I'm the one who was overcharged. I feel like I should stand up for myself and not pay for something I didn't order. Maybe there's a better way to handle this situation without affecting the tip. Like, talking to the manager or explaining my concern without reducing the tip. I'm also wondering about the restaurant's policy. Is it common to charge for water? I thought water was usually complimentary. If they're charging for it, maybe they're trying to increase their revenue, but I don't think it's fair to charge for something as basic as water. So, in the end, I'm conflicted. On one hand, I don't want to pay for something I didn't order, but on the other hand, I don't want to affect the service staff's earnings by leaving a lower tip. Maybe there's a middle ground where I can address the overcharge without reducing the tip. I guess I need to think about what's more important: standing up for what I believe is fair or maintaining a positive relationship with the service staff. It's a tough call, but I think it's worth finding a way to communicate my concerns without penalizing the staff.
